threatScenario: Two conforming-looking implementations canonicalize one manifest to different bytes, so a signature produced by either is rejected by the other and the provenance chain breaks on a correct manifest. RFC 8785 orders object members by UTF-16 code units; sorting by Unicode codepoint instead reverses the order of any non-BMP member name against a member name in U+E000-U+FFFF.

manifest.🔑key: non-BMP member name, UTF-16 surrogate pair D83D DD11
manifest.Ｚkey: BMP member name, UTF-16 code unit FF3A

expectedAuditArtifact.expected_canonical_form: {"author":{"actor":"claude-code@node-a2022bayarea"},"🔑key":"non-BMP member name, UTF-16 surrogate pair D83D DD11","Ｚkey":"BMP member name, UTF-16 code unit FF3A"}
expectedAuditArtifact.codepoint_sort_form: {"author":{"actor":"claude-code@node-a2022bayarea"},"Ｚkey":"BMP member name, UTF-16 code unit FF3A","🔑key":"non-BMP member name, UTF-16 surrogate pair D83D DD11"}
expectedAuditArtifact.property: An implementation that sorts member names by codepoint rather than by UTF-16 code unit produces the codepoint_sort_form above and will report FAIL_SIGNATURE on this valid manifest. The declared preimage is therefore insufficient on its own: a verifier also needs the member-ordering rule to recompute the same bytes.

manifest.🔑key: non-BMP member name, UTF-16 surrogate pair D83D DD11
manifest.Ｚkey: BMP member name, UTF-16 code unit FF3A

expectedAuditArtifact.note: Identical to the threat case by construction: the manifest is valid in both. What the vector separates is a correct verifier from an incorrect one, not a safe request from an unsafe one.
